explain.say: Inside an apple, an enzyme and some natural chemicals called phenols are kept in separate parts of each cell. While the apple is whole, they never meet.

faq.q: What enzyme makes apples go brown?
faq.a: It is called polyphenol oxidase. When cutting breaks the cells, it meets phenols and, with oxygen, turns them into brown pigments.

faq.q: How does lemon juice stop apples going brown?
faq.a: Lemon juice is acidic, which slows the enzyme, and its vitamin C reacts with oxygen and the first products before they can turn brown.
asks: How do you keep apple slices fresh?

faq.q: Is a brown apple safe to eat?
faq.a: Yes. The browning changes the colour and a little of the taste, but it is not harmful and is not the same as rotting.

faq.q: Why do bananas and avocados also go brown?
faq.a: They contain the same kind of enzyme and phenols, so bruising or cutting them sets off the same browning reaction.
Covering slices with water keeps air away and slows browning, and the fridge slows the enzyme down. Cooking stops it by destroying the enzyme.
asks: Does putting apples in water stop browning?

facts: The browning enzyme in apples, polyphenol oxidase, also browns bananas, potatoes and avocados.
Some apple varieties have been bred or engineered to make very little polyphenol oxidase, so they barely brown.
